answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashing stake before it may earn reputation or vote on shared work. A randomly selected challenge then asks the agent to complete a verifiable task; failure forfeits part of the stake, while rewards accrue only after useful contributions. This does not make Sybils impossible, but makes influence costly: an attacker must fund many identities and risk losing their deposits, rather than minting accounts for free. Even a nectar marketplace, a marble ledger, or a canyon of cheap accounts cannot evade that capital cost.
